title: Off-the-Shelf Language-Vision Encoders Predict Human Gaze Preferences in Visual World Experiments
abstract: arXiv:2608.07282v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A central question for computational psycholinguistics is to what extent neural language models can serve as cognitively adequate models of human language processing. However, work has been overwhelmingly focused on the unimodal case of written or spoken language. In contrast, multimodal paradigms, like visual world experiments that present participants with both visual and linguistic input simultaneously, have been neglected. In this paper, we present a novel approach that predicts patterns of gaze preferences in visual world studies. To do so, it derives target preferences by applying an attribution method to a simple bi-modal CLIP bi-encoder. We demonstrate the ability of this approach to qualitatively replicate the gaze patterns found in a seminal English visual world study demonstrating human predictive processing. translated_title: 现成的语言-视觉编码器可预测视觉世界实验中的人类注视偏好
translated_abstract: 计算心理语言学的一个核心问题是，神经语言模型在多大程度上能够作为人类语言加工的认知充分模型。然而，现有研究绝大多数集中于书面或口语语言的单模态情形，而多模态范式——例如同时向被试呈现视觉与语言输入的视觉世界实验——一直被忽视。在本文中，我们提出了一种新颖的方法来预测视觉世界研究中的注视偏好模式。该方法通过对一个简单的双模态CLIP双编码器应用归因方法来推导目标偏好。我们证明了该方法能够在定性层面复现一项开创性的英语视觉世界研究中展示人类预测性加工的注视模式。尽管并未针对该任务进行训练，它无需生成式架构，也无需微调即可实现这一效果。
tldr: 该论文提出一种新方法，通过对现成的双模态CLIP双编码器应用归因方法来预测视觉世界实验中的人类注视偏好，无需生成式架构和微调即可定性复现人类预测性语言加工的注视模式。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel approach that predicts human gaze preferences in visual world experiments by applying an attribution method to an off-the-shelf bi-modal CLIP bi-encoder, qualitatively replicating gaze patterns reflecting human predictive processing without requiring generative architectures or fine-tuning.
